claude.sample_unit: screening examinations (Germany n=1,657,068; UK n=223,603; Sweden n=22,779)

links.outcome: AI integration strategies versus radiologist double-reading screening programme on cancer detection rate, recall, workload
links.effect: Standalone AI achieved non-inferior CDR 6.37 vs programme 6.32 per 1000, recall 3.80 vs 4.11 per 100; decision referral CDR 6.85, recall 3.55, 84% workload reduction.
links.quote: Compared with the German screening programme (CDR 6·32 per 1000 examinations, recall rate 4·11 per 100 examinations), replacement of both readers (standalone AI strategy) achieved a non-inferior CDR of 6·37 (95% CI 6·10-6·64) at a recall rate of 3·80 (95% CI 3·67-3·93), whereas single reader replacement achieved a CDR of 6·49 (6·31-6·67), a recall rate of 4·01 (3·92-4·10), and a 49% workload reduction.

unlisted_practices: Comparing AI integration strategies (standalone replacement, single reader replacement, decision referral, normal triaging) for mammography screening workflow

links.effect: Swedish programme-level decision referral increased CDR by 17·7% without increasing recall and reduced reading workload by 92%.
links.quote: On the Swedish dataset, programme-level decision referral increased the CDR by 17·7% without increasing recall and while reducing reading workload by 92%.

links.effect: Standalone AI CDR 6·37 (95% CI 6·10-6·64) vs German programme 6·32; recall 3·80 vs 4·11.
links.quote: Compared with the German screening programme (CDR 6·32 per 1000 examinations, recall rate 4·11 per 100 examinations), replacement of both readers (standalone AI strategy) achieved a non-inferior CDR of 6·37 (95% CI 6·10-6·64) at a recall rate of 3·80 (95% CI 3·67-3·93), whereas single reader replacement achieved a CDR of 6·49 (6·31-6·67), a recall rate of 4·01 (3·92-4·10), and a 49% workload reduction.

links.effect: UK AI strategies had CDRs 8·24, 8·59, and 8·28 vs programme 8·19; workload reductions 37%, 81%, and 95%.
links.quote: Compared with the UK programme CDR of 8·19, the reader-level, programme-level, and deferral to single reader strategies achieved CDRs of 8·24 (7·82-8·71), 8·59 (8·12-9·06), and 8·28 (7·86-8·71), without increasing recall and while reducing workload by 37%, 81%, and 95%, respectively.

links.effect: Decision referral improved CDR/recall and reduced workload by 84%, 81%, and 92%, but normal triaging was the exception.
links.quote: The decision referral strategies offered the largest improvements in cancer detection rates and reduction in recall rates, and all strategies except normal triaging showed potential to improve screening metrics.

links.outcome: cancer detection rate, recall rate, and workload reduction
links.effect: decision referral improved cancer detection rates and reduced recall rates compared to screening programmes, with workload reductions of 81% to 92%
links.quote: The decision referral strategies offered the largest improvements in cancer detection rates and reduction in recall rates, and all strategies except normal triaging showed potential to improve screening metrics.
